channel.title: Perl Weekly #794
channel.description: Hand-picked news and articles about Perl - Made with love by TabHub(https://tabhub.github.io)

item.title: Perl IDE Developer Survey 2026
item.description: The Perl IDE Survey provides community driven insights into tools, editors, and workflows. It shows the preferred main choices such as Vim and VS Code and metrics on LSP, testing practices, and other main programming tools.
item.author: PerlWeekly

item.title: ANNOUNCE: Perl.Wiki V 1.56, CPAN::MetaCurator V 1.33
item.description: Ron Savage has announced the availability of Perl.Wiki (version 1.56), as well as CPAN::MetaCurator (version 1.33). This new version integrates ChangeLog features into the JSTree menu and also improves the overall appearance of the program's interface.
item.author: ron_savage

item.title: It's Time to Retire Your @cpan.org Email Address
item.description: CPAN authors are reminded by Olaf Alders to stop using their @cpan.org email accounts permanently after the Perl NOC closed the forwarding service earlier this year. The maintenance of correct MetaCPAN profiles and contact information enables the CPAN Security Group to get in touch with maintainers regarding urgent security notifications.
item.author: olaf_alders

item.title: Perl documentation (including POD) with Markdown and Docbook
item.description: Andrew has presented a novel set of CPAN modules made to connect the latest Markdown and DocBook process with traditional Perl POD. The article underscores the sidecar markdown documentation files that get automatically integrated with source files thanks to MakeMaker's goals together with the software for making rich and static sites.
item.author: andrew_speer

item.title: This week in PSC (238) | 2026-10-05
item.description: In the most recent update from the Perl Steering Council (Issue #238), discussions regarding the improvement of @INC handling continue. They also provide an update on the results of monitoring the effects of changes made to the way anonymous subroutines generate line numbers.
item.author: PerlWeekly

item.title: Minion: The Silent Engine That Turns Perl Into a Modern Architecture Platform
item.description: Dani describes how the Minion framework, which is part of Mojolicious, supports background job processing and SQL data storage in Perl applications. This article presents a detailed explanation and proposes Minion as a simpler and better option than heavy queue-based systems using Redis or kinds of enterprise-level job queues.
item.author: dani_otelch

item.title: Peta::NN - Surface Detail
item.description: PetaMem showcases Peta::NN, a zero-dependency neural networking library created from Perl, which can build and train micro-models such as inflection and word category. The post also describes things like modular pipelines, GPU acceleration (using Peta::WebGPU), and tested apps (like accurate German noun pluralisation).
item.author: petamem

item.title: Game::Terminal: Perl game implementations in a terminal
item.description: Robert presents Game::Terminal, a single consolidated CPAN distribution of over twenty terminal-based classic board, card, and arcade games. The post explains how a clean and modular engine design powers both this new CLI menu launcher and an upcoming browser-based gaming platform.
item.author: robert_acock

item.title: The Long Life of WWW::Shorten
item.description: Dave makes observations regarding the history of Perl for 24 years and looks at the history and origins of the URL shortening module suite WWW::Shorten after making corrections since some of the email addresses from that period are now retired.
item.author: dave_cross
